A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AESOP research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution experiments, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, real-world evaluations, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a qualitative comparison of feature inversion using AE and VGG representations.

M1.justification: Both versions pretrain the same autoencoder, freeze it during SR training, and replace pixel loss with distance between decoded AE outputs. Section 4.1 clarifies the existing forward and inverse mappings without changing the architecture, objectives, or procedure.

E1.justification: DF2K training and the bicubic and real-world SR dataset coverage remain unchanged. The new representation diagnostic uses an image from the already-used LSDIR dataset; it does not extend the SR tasks, domains, or degradation scenarios.

E2.justification: VGG becomes an explicitly evaluated comparator to the proposed AE in v2 Figure 10's feature-inversion diagnostic. The comparator sets in the existing SR benchmarks remain unchanged, including the CALGAN and DRCT-based comparisons already present in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds a feature-inversion comparison using AE and VGG features from a specified LSDIR image. Existing training budgets, patch sizes, metrics, and preprocessing remain unchanged. The new diagnostic's detailed inversion settings are not specified.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 10 adds a qualitative case study examining which reconstruction details AE and VGG representations preserve. Existing component ablations, alternative-AE tests, frequency analyses, loss maps, and trade-off analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added qualitative diagnostic introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–7 are unchanged; v1 Tables 8 and 9 become v2 Tables 9 and 8 with their scores retained. Existing appendix curves and image examples also match. New Figure 10 illustrates better structural preservation through AE features than through VGG features.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the expectation defining the prediction centroid from an expectation over y to one over the prediction yhat. It also specifies that Equation 2 applies to L2, replacing the imprecise 'Gaussian prior on L' statement. The remaining mathematical development is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: analyzing pixel-loss conflicts and proposing AE-based fidelity supervision that preserves perceptual variation. Wording changes do not alter these claims' scope.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix D expands the explanation that VGG features discard reconstruction-critical information and argues that perceptual loss cannot serve as a standalone reconstruction loss. The existing Manga109 failure discussion, AE dependence, and perception-distortion limitations are retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the architecture, initialization, optimizer, learning rate, training iterations, evaluation settings, BasicSR implementation, and GPU disclosures. No substantive implementation recipe for the new inversion diagnostic or new code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. However, v2 expands AESOP's positioning relative to VGG-based perceptual losses, emphasizing preservation of reconstruction information and suitability as a reconstruction objective beyond the earlier objective and bottleneck comparison.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose corrections, clarifies AE pretraining, expands the perceptual-loss discussion, and reorganizes appendix discussions and visualization material. It also corrects affiliation/contact text and adds acknowledgements; the main narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: The supplementary prose is extensively reformatted from one column to two, with multiple tables and figures relocated or resized. Tables 8 and 9 exchange order, and the spectral visualization moves before the trade-off curves. v2 also revises Figure 2, adds panel labels to Figure 6, and introduces Figure 10.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through the Section 3 corrections and makes the distinction from perceptual loss more concrete through the expanded discussion and new feature-inversion illustration. The gains are limited: the method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged, and the new diagnostic lacks detailed inversion settings. Its broad conclusion about standalone perceptual losses also exceeds what the single illustrated case establishes.
